campaign.protocol_note: Adaptive arms with dual step 5 were added on 2026-10-03 after the pre-registered step 100 ran away (failure rate 1 in the first rollouts, multiplier past 10^4); the step-100 runs are reported as well. Tank-20 arms (prices 0 and 0.5) were added after the tank-21 arms turned out to be respected by most campaign controllers, so that (P7) is tested at a tank the controller cannot respect, as in the pilots.

additions_2026_11_10.note: Added on 2026-11-10, after the results of the stored runs, to examine one reading of them: a fixed price changes the returned policy only when the price times the risk without a price, m q_{beta,H}(pi_0)/(1-beta), exceeds what the learner resolves (the return varies between seeds by about 17), and a charge above the return of an episode (m above about 0.48) degrades the policy. Stated before these runs: at tanks 21 and 20 the price 0.05 puts about 5 and 7 units of return at stake and no order of the exhaustion probabilities is expected; the price 0.15 puts about 15 and 20 at stake, at the spread; the price 2 is expected to degrade the policies as at tank 22. At tanks 23 and 24 the risk without a price is expected to be small (2 percent in the one pilot seed at tank 24), so that the price 0.5 puts less than the spread at stake and no systematic fall of exhaustion is expected. All other settings are those of the stage: continued training for warm_steps from the unconstrained controller of the same seed, the same learner settings, 1000 evaluation episodes.

crash-campaign.note: Added on 2026-11-14. The whole study is trained again under a revised failure. (1) The loss of the lander (a crash, or leaving the frame) is a failure and is charged like an empty tank (option crash_fails of lunar.py). Reason: in the stage campaign a price above about 0.17 makes an empty tank cost more than a crash (the charge is about 590 m, the native crash penalty is 100), and the returned policies exchange exhaustion for crashes; at the tank of 20 units and the price 0.5 the exhaustion frequency falls from 0.27 to 0.12 and the crash frequency rises from 0.07 to 0.25. (2) The tank can fail only before touchdown, the first frame at which a leg touches the ground; after it an empty tank switches the engines off and the episode continues to a landing or to the loss of the lander (option tank_until_touchdown). Reason: in the stage campaign a leg had touched the ground before the tank ran out in 71 percent of the exhausted episodes at the tank of 20 units without a price and in 97 percent at the price 0.5. All other settings are those of the stage campaign: the same 23 configurations and five seeds, continued training for warm_steps from the unconstrained controller of the same seed (stage campaign, trained on the native task and not trained again), the same learner settings, 1000 evaluation episodes. The adaptive configurations keep their tolerances and dual steps; their failure rate now includes the loss of the lander, which the unconstrained controllers incur in 2 to 6 percent of the episodes. The stage campaign is kept unchanged as a record. A first start of this stage on the same day with rule (1) alone was stopped after five runs, which are not kept.

crash-pilot-norm.note: Tuning pilot of 2026-11-14 at the tank of 20 units, under the failure of the stage crash-campaign. Finding that led to it: with the learner settings of the stage campaign (rewards not normalized) the failure probability after 3 million steps rises with the price (0.16, 0.18, 0.22, 0.59 at the prices 0, 0.15, 0.5, 2). The training traces show a delay and not another optimum: every run starts at the failure rate 1, since the unconstrained controller empties the tank before touchdown, and the fall of the failure rate begins later the larger the charge (at the price 2 after 60 to 100 percent of the training), and no run has levelled off. This pilot changes one learner setting, the normalization of the rewards by a running estimate of the standard deviation of the return (VecNormalize of Stable-Baselines3, rewards only), so that the size of the charge does not set the size of the value targets. Everything else is as in the stage crash-campaign.

sac-pilot.note: Pilot of 2026-11-14 at the tank of 20 units with another learner, the soft actor-critic of Stable-Baselines3, under the failure of the stage crash-campaign. Reason: with the proximal policy optimization of the stage campaign, continued from the unconstrained controller, every run starts at the failure rate 1 and has not levelled off after 3 million steps, so the outcomes compare learning speeds (stages crash-campaign and crash-pilot-norm at this tank). The soft actor-critic is trained from scratch for 500,000 steps under each configuration, with the discount of the study (0.999), rewards normalized, and otherwise the reference settings of the RL Baselines3 Zoo for this lander task (batch 256, buffer 10^6, tau 0.01, one gradient step per step, 10,000 steps before learning, networks 400-300, automatic entropy coefficient; learning rate 3e-4 constant). The paper's results do not depend on the learner, which enters only through the optimization error.
sac-pilot.result_note: Stopped after its first batch (no price and the price 0.5). From scratch the learner did not find the landing in 2 of 5 seeds without a price and in 3 of 5 at the price 0.5 (failure probabilities 0.98, 0.16, 0.99, 0.13, 0.19 and 0.99, 0.84, 0.96, 0.11, 0.21). Across all runs of the stages crash-campaign, crash-pilot-norm and sac-pilot at this tank the stopped utility falls with the failure probability (about 245 minus 150 times it): the task has no trade-off between utility and risk for a price to act on.

fuelprice-pilot.note: Pilot of 2026-11-14: the utility charges 5 per unit of fuel in place of the native 1 (option fuel_price of lunar.py), at the tank of 24 units, under the failure of the stage crash-campaign, with the learner of the stage crash-pilot-norm (continued proximal policy optimization, rewards normalized). Reason: see the result note of the stage sac-pilot; with valuable fuel the utility rewards late braking and thin reserves, so there is a trade-off between utility and risk that a price on failure can act on. The tank of 24 units is chosen so that the starting controller does not fail in every episode.
fuelprice-pilot.result_note: Failure probability 0.097, 0.077, 0.058, 0.046 at the prices 0, 0.15, 0.5, 2 (means over five seeds); landed 0.901, 0.921, 0.941, 0.952; median fuel 19.6, 19.9, 19.9, 21.1; stopped utility 162.5, 163.5, 166.2, 158.4. The order is as wanted in the means; per seed the failure probability falls in 2, 3 and 3 of 5 seeds, so the effect is of the size of the differences between seeds.

fuelprice-pilot-8.note: As the stage fuelprice-pilot, with 8 per unit of fuel in the utility, to see whether a larger value of fuel makes the effect of the price larger than the differences between seeds.
fuelprice-pilot-8.result_note: Failure probability 0.070, 0.095, 0.070, 0.094 at the prices 0, 0.15, 0.5, 2; median fuel 18.8, 18.9, 19.8, 20.4; stopped utility 116, 111, 109, 102. No fall of the failure probability.

fuelprice-pilot-12.note: As the stage fuelprice-pilot, with 12 per unit of fuel in the utility, to see whether a larger value of fuel makes the effect of the price larger than the differences between seeds.
fuelprice-pilot-12.result_note: Failure probability 0.177, 0.110, 0.065, 0.127 at the prices 0, 0.15, 0.5, 2 (it falls in 4, 5 and 3 of 5 seeds); landed 0.821, 0.886, 0.932, 0.870; median fuel 18.1, 19.1, 19.8, 20.4; stopped utility 35.9, 35.3, 35.4, 20.9. One seed (72003) learns slowly at every price and ends at 0.43 at the price 2; several runs have not levelled off.
fuelprice-pilot-12.grid_note: The prices 0.75, 1 and 1.25 were added on 2026-11-14 to fill the range between 0.5 and 2; the price 2 may be dropped from the final design if its large charge keeps disturbing the learner.

fuelprice-12-long.note: As the stage fuelprice-pilot-12 (12 per unit of fuel in the utility, tank 24), with three times the training (9 million steps), to see the outcomes after the runs have levelled off.
fuelprice-12-long.result_note: Failure probability 0.067, 0.030, 0.025, 0.013 at the prices 0, 0.15, 0.5, 2 (it falls in 4, 5 and 5 of 5 seeds); landed 0.931, 0.969, 0.975, 0.987; median fuel 18.1, 18.1, 18.7, 20.3; stopped utility 55.3, 64.3, 58.3, 40.6. The priced runs have levelled off; without a price two seeds (72003, 72005) are still improving at the end, which is why the utility without a price is below that at the price 0.15. The price 2 trains without trouble at this length.

fuelprice-pilot-16.note: As the stage fuelprice-pilot, with 16 per unit of fuel in the utility. At this value a landing with about 18 units of fuel costs about as much as the landing is worth, so that without a price the utility may prefer to give up the lander.
fuelprice-pilot-16.grid_note: The prices 0.75, 1 and 1.25 were added on 2026-11-14 to fill the range between 0.5 and 2; the price 2 may be dropped from the final design if its large charge keeps disturbing the learner.

fuelprice-pilot-20.note: As the stage fuelprice-pilot, with 20 per unit of fuel in the utility. At this value a landing with about 18 units of fuel costs about as much as the landing is worth, so that without a price the utility may prefer to give up the lander.
fuelprice-pilot-20.grid_note: The prices 0.75, 1 and 1.25 were added on 2026-11-14 to fill the range between 0.5 and 2; the price 2 may be dropped from the final design if its large charge keeps disturbing the learner.

fuelprice-20-long.note: The design with 20 per unit of fuel in the utility (tank 24, failure of the stage crash-campaign, continued proximal policy optimization with normalized rewards), all seven prices, trained for 15 million steps so that the runs level off (the stage fuelprice-12-long showed that 9 million steps settle the priced runs and not yet all runs without a price).
fuelprice-20-long.result_note: Failure probability 0.359, 0.050, 0.032, 0.021, 0.021, 0.015, 0.012 at the prices 0, 0.15, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 2 (it falls in 5 of 5 seeds at every price); landed 0.640, 0.950, 0.968, 0.978, 0.978, 0.984, 0.987; median fuel 14.4, 17.2, 17.8, 18.1, 17.9, 18.8, 18.5; stopped utility -63.4, -58.5, -67.7, -74.9, -69.2, -88.7, -78.8. No tank runs empty before touchdown. The training failure rate is flat over the last three tenths of the training at every price. Without a price the seeds end at 0.09, 0.05, 0.47, 0.34, 0.85 with utilities between -53 and -78: at this value of fuel landing and giving up the lander are worth about the same.

fuelprice-20-const.note: Convergence check of the stage fuelprice-20-long (2026-11-16): the same design at the prices 0, 0.5 and 2 with a constant learning rate (3e-4) in place of the rate decayed linearly to zero. A flat end of a trace under a decaying learning rate does not show convergence, since the decay stops a run in any case; the outcomes under a constant rate show whether the levels of the stage depend on the schedule. From 2026-11-16 this stage, with all seven prices, is the final design; the stage fuelprice-20-long is its comparison under the decayed rate.
fuelprice-20-const.result_note: First three prices (2026-11-16): with a price the outcomes equal those under the decayed rate (failure probability 0.030 against 0.032 at the price 0.5, 0.021 against 0.012 at the price 2; median fuel 17.6 against 17.8 and 18.5 against 18.5; stopped utility -68 against -68 and -83 against -79). Without a price they do not: failure probability 0.715 against 0.359, median fuel 6.2 against 14.4, stopped utility -38 against -63. Two seeds end at failure probability 1 with half a unit of fuel and utilities -15 and -11, far above the utility of the policies that land (-53 to -64). The runs without a price under the decayed rate had been stopped by the decay; at 20 per unit of fuel the utility is highest when the lander is given up. The constant rate is therefore the learner setting of the final design, and the other four prices are added to this stage.
fuelprice-20-const.grid_note: The prices 0.05 and 0.1 were added on 2026-11-16, after the runs without a price under the constant learning rate gave up the lander: their charges at the failing frame are about 30 and 59, and the utility of giving up the lander exceeds that of landing by about 40 to 50, so the change from giving up to landing is expected between them.
fuelprice-20-const.result_note_all_prices: Seven prices (2026-11-16): failure probability 0.715, 0.071, 0.030, 0.036, 0.040, 0.045, 0.021 at the prices 0, 0.15, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 2 (it falls in 5 of 5 seeds at every price); median fuel 6.2, 17.1, 17.6, 18.0, 17.9, 18.5, 18.5; stopped utility -38.4, -64.5, -68.0, -71.8, -74.5, -81.9, -83.1. The utility falls at every step. Among the prices the failure probabilities differ by less than their spread over the seeds (1 to 4 percentage points), which is larger than under the decayed rate, since under a constant rate the policy keeps moving.

fuelprice-20-adaptive.note: The adaptive multiplier in the design of the stage fuelprice-20-long (2026-11-16): the failing frame receives minus the multiplier, which is raised after every rollout by the dual step times the excess of the rollout's failure rate over the tolerance. Tolerances 0.05 and 0.02, attained in the stage fuelprice-20-long at the fixed prices 0.15 and 0.75 to 1 (charges of about 88 and 440 to 590). Dual steps 5 and 20. At the start the continued controller fails in 40 to 100 percent of the episodes, so the multiplier rises fast in the first rollouts and falls only slowly afterwards, by the step times the small shortfall below the tolerance. Constant learning rate, as in the final design.

fuelprice-12-grid-long.note: The design with 12 per unit of fuel in the utility, all seven prices, 15 million steps: the milder case next to the stage fuelprice-20-long, for the Online Resource. Constant learning rate, as in the final design.

fuelprice-20-const-30m.note: Convergence check of the final design (2026-11-16): the prices 0, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.5 under the constant learning rate with twice the training (30 million steps), to see where the runs without a price end and whether the runs at the two smallest prices, at which giving up the lander has about the value of landing, stay with the policies that land. The prices 0.05 and 0.1 were added in the evening of 16 November.
fuelprice-20-const-30m.result_note: No price: failed 77.5 % [100, 3.9, 100, 98.7, 85.1], utility -27; four of the five seeds end near giving up the lander, one stays with landing. Price 0.5: failed 2.4 % [2.1, 2.1, 2.2, 4.3, 1.5], fuel 17.4, utility -59, against 2.5 %, 17.2 and -58 in the design. The traces contain those of fuelprice-20-const (same seeds).

fuelprice-20-anneal.note: Final phase of the final design (2026-11-16): every run of the stage fuelprice-20-const is continued for 5 million steps with the learning rate decayed linearly from 3e-4 to zero. The constant rate lets the runs without a price reach the policies that give up the lander, and the decay at the end removes the movement of the policy that a constant rate leaves. The learning rate of the final design is thus constant for 15 million steps and then decayed to zero over 5 million.

fuelprice-20-adaptive-anneal.note: Final phase of the adaptive configurations of the final design (2026-11-16): every run of the stage fuelprice-20-adaptive is continued for 5 million steps with the learning rate decayed linearly from 3e-4 to zero and the multiplier held at the value at which that run ended, so that every run of the study has the same learning-rate schedule. The multiplier is not updated in this phase, since a policy that no longer moves cannot answer it.

fuelprice-12-grid-anneal.note: Final phase of the milder case with fuel at 12 per unit (2026-11-16): every run of the stage fuelprice-12-grid-long is continued for 5 million steps with the learning rate decayed linearly from 3e-4 to zero, the schedule of the final design.

formulations-const.note: Pilot across formulations of the lander problem (2026-11-17, run on Roihu). Two families. ledger-R*: the utility is a ledger, with the revenue R paid once when the lander comes to rest on the pad and fuel at 1 per unit; the benchmark's potential enters the training reward only, in the form that leaves the objective unchanged. bench-c*: the benchmark's reward (payments for progress and 100 at rest) with fuel at c per unit, as in the stages fuelprice-*. Tanks of 18 and 24 units. The price is set so that a failure near frame 100 is charged k times what a landing earns (R, or 290 for the benchmark's reward), k = 0, 0.5, 2, 8: the lost vehicle is worth k landings. Learner and schedule as in the stages fuelprice-20-const and fuelprice-20-anneal.

formulations-anneal.note: Final phase of the stage formulations-const, with the learning rate decayed linearly to zero.

formulations-test.note: Test of the stage formulations-const on Roihu (500,000 steps), to measure the speed and the memory of a run before the pilot is submitted.
